item.title: The Flight of the Koalas: Re: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Veralta. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ LBL
- LBL

Wilpena Pound

This might not be as well known a place to people outside Australia. You might want to add a clarifier after?

Sightings of "flying serpents" are to be quickly verified and acted upon.

“acted upon” is slightly vague. Do you want to give a more specific hint so we can understand the anomaly a little better?

The Foundation History Department is mandated to research texts and information

The tense here is a little inconsistent when compared to the previous sentences. I would remove “is mandated to” and simply put “will” to keep with the clinical tone.

to collect pertinent information.

Again, being specific in the conprocs goes a long way. What kind of information should the Foundation look out for? This adds to our understanding of the scp in the long run.

during 2022

Sounds a little off. You would say “during a year”, but not a specific one. Would change to “in 2022”.

two years after severe bushland fires within the region

Missing an “occurred” after “fires”.

Compiled data indicates a severe decline in population density, upwards of nearly 2,000 per week.

Nitpick, but the second part of this sentence doesn’t link to the first. “2,000” refers to the actual number, not the population density.

It is to be noted that the surviving koala population at this point numbered approximately 62,000.

The past tense of “numbered” indicates that the Foundation is writing from a place of the future? Sorry, just wanted to clarify.

Additionally, testimonies from zoos across and outside the continent indicate that their koalas have also disappeared, despite all efforts to contain or track them.

This was slightly confusing to read. Do you just mean “internationally” or “globally”?

Uluru, Wilpena Pound, Black Mountain2, Arnhem Land, and the Grampian National Park.

Again, these might be entirely foreign terms for those not familiar with Australian Geography. You might want to add qualifiers like “near Sydney” or in “New South Wales”.

Heavy rainfall would occur in tandem

Tenses need to be more consistent, I think. You’re switching between present and future perfect tense, which muddies the viewer’s sense of time.

as SCP-5870 continuously occurs.

A little awkward. You mean to say “at the rate SCP-5870 continues to occur”?

The 2020 bushfires had burned 24 percent of the eucalyptus trees, while approximately 60,000 koalas have been recorded as casualties. 84 percent of survivors have severe burns on their paws, while 31 percent had suffered from dehydration and starvation.

I’m not sure this entire section should be under the “Description” section, as it’s additional context for the anomaly, and not about the anomaly itself. You could re-classify this section as your Discovery log.

SCP-5870-1 instances, despite numerous

“being numerous”.

share striking similaries.

“similarities”. And also, similarities to what? Each other?

bullroarers

Second occurrence of a foreign term without additional context.

These were subsequently fed by the entities to arriving SCP-5870-1 instances

This is happening quite fast, making it hard to keep track of who is who. “These” meaning the nuts? “the entities” here refer to the koalas? I would break up the description and add a little more detail for pacing.

After five minutes, they flew at high speeds

Indicate direction?

which would then hold onto them

“hold” => “cling”. Might want to also specify which parts of the snakes they hold onto.

where a large levitating island, referred to as SCP-5870-2, was discovered.

Whoa, whoa. Why wasn’t this noticed before?

It is to be noted that 40 percent of the island's surface is composed of a lake.

I would remove the “It is to be noted” as this is not something particularly noteworthy.

They then reach a small lake, wherein the main dome is located at its center.

This is confusing. Is the small lake located at the center of the dome? Or is the main dome at the center?

Some of the koala groups make their way to the smaller domes, which are not located in the the lake.

I thought they were deposited at the smaller domes first? “the” is repeated.

koalas living onto them

Unclear what you mean here.

as they are spectated by other koalas.

“as” meaning “because” they are spectated? Meaning unclear.

It is notably

“notably” -> “notable”.

dyed white and yellow.

Again, why is this noteworthy?

The koalas enter the dome.

I thought we were already inside the main dome. Best to clarify earlier where the drone footage starts, and where we’re headed.

manipulated in get fleshy materials

Sorry? Is there a typo here?

After it leaves the SCP-5870-2 duplicate at Mount Warning, SCP-5870-3 has collected approximately 5,600 more koalas.

The sentence structure here is convoluted. Meaning unclear.

the Foundation has listed koalas as critically endangered

Ah? Are we in a Broken Masquerade scenario? Why is the Foundation assuring the public?

Overall, I enjoyed this exploration log, though I felt it went on a little too long and didn’t understand the significance of certain events (like the koalas and kangeroos fighting). You might also want to clarify the description to make it clear what we’re seeing, when.

mitigated these through engineering solutions.

“these” refers to? If it’s the flooding, then the tense should be changed.

10 percent of its national budget to it

“it” refers to?

approximately 115.31 million tons

tonnes of what?

35 Small Modular Reactors14.

The footnote should come after the period.

the TIMES magazine

Do you mean “Time Magazine”?

Closely cooperating with aboriginal groups such as Bundjalung, Eora, and Gamilaaray, greenery restoration programs in New South Wales and Queensland have also been successful

The subject of the sentence is not clear – who is the one “closely cooperating”?

Foundation task forces quickly mobilize. Fortunately, most Australians were celebrating the New Year inside their homes.

I don’t see the link between both sentences?

turn over a new leaf

Personally, this is a highly cliqued phrase, though I can’t say much else if it’s officially a part of lore. Consider rephrasing to simply “turn over” or “turn themselves over” to get the same effect.

+ Overall
- Overall

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?

Well, yeah. It was a wild ride. I’m not familiar with Aboriginal culture (like, at all), and seeing these stories come to life was eye-opening. I just hoped to understand their significance a little more. You’ve clearly done our research and included many references to the culture and origin stories. The main issue (if it really is one in the first place) is outsiders like me don’t really see the significance of the minute events / symbols / objects.

I do like the overarching narrative though of nature taking climate change into its own hands. It’s a strong and relevant message. My major concern would be the deemphasis here on the Foundation’s role in the entire article. Basically, we’re just left as bystanders throughout the entire event, right? Which is fine if that’s what you’re going for, but removes any agency and tension from the narrative.

2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?

Yup, as mentioned above, A good amount of detail included. Just needs to be further explained and the description clarified (who, where and when we are).

3. Does it sound too preachy?

Nope. I think the lesson is clear but not overbearing.

4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

Perhaps I don’t understand the lore and beliefs in the first place. You could be more explicit in this regard, for example, providing an actual story or myth at the beginning, besides just the stone carving.

I also wasn’t clear throughout how the aboriginal community fit into the scp. There’s a passing reference to them creating posters to create awareness, but where do they fit into the story? Wouldn’t it be cool if you could show them being facilitators / active defenders of the entities as the anomalies occur. But again, I don’t want to prescribe a cultural stance for them.

Overall, I’m tending towards an up-vote. The writing is mostly clear, as are the notes and themes you seek to hit.

Thanks for sharing this with us!

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

item.title: Air Reconditioning Unit: Re: Air Reconditioning Unit
item.content:encoded:
Hi, thank you for your critique!

+ My response.
- Close response.

I’m not sure how to answer those questions and it’s mostly because I struggle with expressing the thoughts in my head. I have the answers and they make sense to me but writing them down is hard. But I’m going to try.

The whole piece is about the realisation that there’s an SCP that’s made fixing climate change kinda moot, it’s added it’s own irreversible and irrecoverable damage to the climate and that the world is kinda fucked. That’s what I want the reader to come away with.

I don’t know how I can make a character someone can relate to in this kind of piece. I thought I had at least on some small level. This one I really don’t know how to fix.

I want this to say a lot of things, like “hi I am a new writer but I want to be a part of this amazing community” or “this is something I have put time and effort and love into.” It’s probably not the right answer to that question but it’s the answer that feels right to me. This is my first SCP, when I’m gone this will remain as my legacy. I want this to be something people can point to and say “yep, that guy did that. It’s okay I guess.” That’s what I want it to say.

But again that’s not the answer you probably want, so let me try again. I love this SCP because it has potential. I make several references to another function of the object, which is functionally identical to what is described in the article except instead of turning oxygen into helium it turns it into carbon dioxide or water vapour, with the complexity going up the higher the input number. I want it to say there’s more to this, to make people think and imagine.

I did kinda stupidly think that maybe this could’ve been something that other people could collaborate on, creating and adding things to a list of what this SCP could make. But fears of it being compared to other open collaboration SCPs killed that idea. The testing log is the remnant of that I suppose, turned into an attempt to channel a narrative that admittedly has failed. I do understand that it’s a very dry narrative, and ditching the logs has been advised before. But I honestly don’t know how else to channel and describe a narrative through this kind of fiction, I’ve never written anything like an SCP article before so it’s all foreign to me.

item.title: Star Euthanizer: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
{Placeholder}

On to the critique ->
– hide block

SPaG

On 28 August 1903, Foundation personnel educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX through a telescope near the Orion Arm.

This suggests that the telescope was situated in the Orion's Arm spiral arm, rather than the object was located in that sector. Additionally, "astrology" is defined by Merriam-Webster as "the divination of the supposed influences of the stars and planets on human affairs and terrestrial events by their positions and aspects". I believe the word you are looking for is "astronomy".

"sighted" is also defined as "able to see : not blind." Perhaps "observed".

Consistency/Flow

All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This could be cleaned up a bit to be more specific. It is unclear which standard procedure is being followed. Furthermore, I would assume that all deep space observations would be closely monitored by the SCPF as a matter of course.

The production and trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel are present.

This is also jumbled and unclear. What is this meant to prevent?

All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records.

I have a personal preference for utilizing the .aic convention. In this case, your AI would become Binary_Star.aic. I think it looks cleaner than "name", in that it specifies an entity rather than a "supposed" entity. It's all in the implication.

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft ever observed by the Foundation.

Non-human or non-terrestrial? Or did this observation predate Sputnik and the other Earth-based spacecraft?

Closing Remarks

There are significant errors throughout this piece, what is represented here are just a few examples. The idea is a sound one and I think the additional story told throughout the listpages is interesting. However, there are a lot of sentence structure and word choice errors that make this difficult to read.

Ping me on IRC at your leisure and we can go over more of them if you'd like.

item.title: A Wholesome Gift: A Wholesome Gift
item.content:encoded:
Sandbox link, clocking in at around 2k words.

+ Spoilers?
- Close

The main plot follows the story of Xasbo, a guy who adores cats, until at one of the festivals, he unknowingly consumes his own cat in part due to a tradition in some parts of China which practise the culture of eating cat meat, leading to his disillusionment. The practice itself isn't widely practised, and it's more centered within the Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, so the latter was the first pick of where the massacre happened. After the villagers die, the place somehow got the anomalous power to serve as a place for housing cats.

You can probably say he's more of the extreme of the extreme, PETA activist who cares nothing for humankind.

Main concerns are SPaG, whether the interview is a huge exposition dump, whether Xasbo's personality can mirror more of a subtly psychopathic character, and whether it ends on a sufficiently spooky note in contrast to Xasbo's view of a literal massacre as a festive occasion for the cats.

item.title: The Flight of the Koalas: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Word Count: 2,371

Link: http://scpdsandbox.wikidot.com/veraltanic-page-3-0

Hello everyone! This is Veralta once again completing a draft that I hope to publish as a New Year's gift! I have written a social commentary about koalas, how they and the aboriginal Australians have been affected by the bushland fires, and how people should be more ecologically-minded. I also featured a trip throughout Australia's rich culture and locations, with several of the article's parts being based on Dreamtime1 lore.

Note: I have tried to make the parts of the article that I have based on Dreamtime to be as least abstract as possible, and clear. If there are questions or ambiguity that you can find about them, feel free to mention it in the critique!

Here are the points that I want to be reviewed:

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?
2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?
3. Does it sound too preachy?
4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

All in all, I hope you enjoy this SCP in time for the New Year (and a new leaf for all of us)! Thank you to those who will review this!

Footnotes
1. Umbrella term for aboriginal Australian beliefs.
2. I have researched this part as much as possible, so I would like to not screw up something here.

item.title: Air Reconditioning Unit: Re: Air Reconditioning Unit
item.content:encoded:
Overall:

  • Primarily my problem with this draft is the complete lack of a narrative. This is a series of test logs and observations concerning the anomaly in overly detailed manner. What its missing is an exploration of themes or a narrative arc. Ask yourself:
    • what you want the reader to come away with from this story and
    • if it might be better with someone to relate to…
    • also why is this anomaly interesting to you? Other than it being a fan that changes the molecular makeup of the atmosphere around it… what is it you want to say?

As it stands right now, this is very dry.

  • in terms of small edits, I think you should do away with the testing logs. I think you could summarize the logs in a paragraph in a sub-section labelled “Testing Results” and it would be more efficient. Right now they’re bloat to be cut in my opinion.

item.title: Star Euthanizer: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
Because Quad has already given you his once over, I will be going more in depth with the tone. I can already say I agree with what Quad has said, so I will be expanding on that. Without further ado!

It's time for some critique.
Hope it helps.

Page one

All telescopes capable of deep-space astrophotography are monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This sentence reads a little weird to me. I would recommend changing it. Also keep in mind that you will need to change these on the other pages as well.

"All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure."

The production and selling of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is present.

Just a couple of word changes would hep this flow a bit better.

"The production and selling trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is are present.

All images of SCP-XXXX are intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must be administered Class B amnestics.

Same with this one.

"All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must Those who witness the anomaly are to be administered Class B amnestics.

Page two

The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take a sample.

I would change this slightly.

"The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take difficulty in acquiring a sample.

SCP-XXXX is the object where the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

Just one word.

"SCP-XXXX is the object where that the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a telescope.

I know you said that you would change this, but I think it should stay this way. Adds a bit of historical accuracy that gives this article a nice flavor. There is one change though.

"On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a with his telescope."

The Foundation administered him with amnestics. Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

This sentence can be structured in a better way.

"The Foundation He was administered him with amnestics. , however due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness."

the Foundation decided to let von Zeppelin invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him as manual laborers.

Some more suggestions.

"the Foundation decided to let allow von Zeppelin to invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him planted as manual laborers."

It was anticipated that von Zeppelin eventually would develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX.

I would switch the words ""eventually" and "would" in this sentence.

"It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX."

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX

I feel like you could cut some of this sentence. Sense I would assume researchers searching for SCP-XXXX know a thing or two about astrology.

"On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX-"

Page three

Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1.

"may" doesn't sound very clinical. I would recommend changing this to "are allowed to".

"Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may are allowed to use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1.

This can be trimmed down some.

"SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX that serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which age nor origin have been successfully investigated.

One word change here.

"SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which whose age nor origin have been successfully investigated."

-and store it inside of SCP-XXXX.

Don't think the "of" fits there.

"and store it inside of SCP-XXXX."

SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes.

I think you can trim some fat here because you can already infer that SCP-XXXX-1 is knowledgeable about space.

"SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap capable of leaping several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes."

Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal.

Some trimming.

"Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal."

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

| CONNECTION BROKEN MANUALLY
| END HISTORY

I love this. That is why I recommend cutting everything after this. Like Quad said, I like the idea of a good god patrolling space protecting us, but I feel like this would be a far more impactful ending.

All in all I like this article a lot. To answer the questions you proposed on the forum I will say that the 2nd page is fine, your dialogue is great, and I love the twist. The one thing I would recommend thinking about is a way of making the text that has been added over the various iterations of the article pop out more. I have seen articles change the color of new text to blue or red, and I think it could work with this. I would also recommend getting some more critique. This is very close to something great, but there is probably things Quad and I have missed. I hope this was helpful and good luck.

item.title: Star Euthanizer: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Page 1

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft observed by the Foundation.

As in the first ever spacecraft they ever witnessed or just the first one they witnessed for this SCP? Confused by the wording here.

Considering this is a listpages SCP, I know there's more to come and the first page gives so little info, it serves as a good, 'wait, something isn't right…' page, if you know what I mean. Even without the knowledge of listpages, I think it's still just 'off' enough to give the reader the sense that something isn't right.

The clinical is a bit iffy, though. I apologise that I'm doing a more 'general thoughts' crit and not a true in-depth LBL.

Mainly the bits that bothered me were:

new telescope parts like refractors

I feel like 'such as' would be better than 'like'

SCP-XXXX has a frame in the form between a cylinder and an oblate spheroid.

'between a' is what sounds sub-clinical to me. I'm sure there's a better word to use there…sadly, I'm not that great at clinical tone either, so I kinda…can't think of a suitable replacement for that :U

On the bottom side is a small outer room

The adjective 'small' is what bothers me, as I've read somewhere that most adjectives aren't clinical.

Page 2

Immediately, I find myself significantly more intrigued by this page. I know you said you had problems with Page 2, but I really like it so far.

Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will make said star disappear by unknown means.

'make said star disappear' is vastly unclinical.

How does it make them disappear? By touch?

If so, 'Upon contact with SCP-XXXX-1, stars will immediately vanish. How this occurs is currently unknown.' would be better. But again, I'm no clinical tone pro.

Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

That…is such a fucking cool headcanon you thought of. I love this touch. A lot. Zeppelins are the vague hint towards this SCPs existence. I think that's brilliant.

Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin represents SCP-XXXX the most accurate.

'Currently, SCP-XXXX is most accurately represented by the LZ 127 Zeppelin.'

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX near the Orion Arm. Upon showing von Zeppelin their findings, it was confirmed that this was indeed the same object he saw 30 years ago. He was then administered amnestics again, this time resulting in the permanent loss of his memories of SCP-XXXX.

I would just remove this bit. No way the Foundation would show someone an anomaly only to re-amnesticize them again. I don't buy it. Also, we already know that SCP-XXXX is confirmed to be what he saw, so this is unnecessary and repeats info we already know.

Page 2 is pretty good so far. Definitely a good jump from Page 1. I'll go ahead and read Page 3 and I'll let you know how it stacks up.

Page 3

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 on board

'SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1.'

Also, I really like this bit. This definitely wasn't something I saw coming.

ALSO, HAVE YOU THOUGH OF A NAME YET?

Thought*

YOU HAVE ALWAYS GIVEN ME THE SAME NAME.

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

That was a twist and a half and I fucking love it and it genuinely gives me motivation to continue my own ambitious as hell listpages SCP.

Thank you for sharing this draft with me.

As for the falling action with the O5 sending Glen the godspeed message…idk how to feel about that.

I really like the idea of an anomaly that can't be contained and is universally recognized as good, but at the same time, idk if this is the most realistic reaction the O5 would have.

Either way, the implications, Glen, and the twist at the end is all superb.

Even with the issues I stated above, that twist at the end would have easily earned my upvote.

I think it all works as a whole, just need polish in all the right areas and you're golden.

I didn't stay to deeply examine the dialogue further, but it's definitely improving significantly.

Either way, I hope I helped. Good luck with the rest of this skip, dude. You got this.

👍

item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I don't really like this as a whole; or, rather, I like what it's trying to be more than I like what it is. As written, the story is too static: too much of -2's growth is elided or not able to be shown, and so it just feels…not very interesting.

Like, consider: the way the reader learns that -2 has learnt that he's the source of his power, not the toys, is from -2 just…saying it? There's no like, process of -2 learning this or trying to figure out how it works; and so it feels underwhelming: it's not like, a triumphant, climactic moment of character growth because like, there's no struggle to get there, or even anything we're shown that gradually leads that way. It doesn't really land from just being interesting either because the description explicitly tells us this is the case.

Equally, his growth as a person is elided: we see him being really sad in the tests but there's no real escalation for the sadness or anything, and because the tests are so detached from -2's emotional state, we don't really emphasise with him, so -2 doesn't feel like it's him reaching a breaking point so much as it feels like just a random point. But moving on from there, we don't see any of his recovery, or his struggle to become less suicidal or any of that growth, so it doesn't really land right.

And since neither of these things land properly, the whole thing just feels…passive and uninteresting. It feels almost like we're getting a slice of life story except without any of the charm you can pack into one, and so I'm just…left feeling underwhelmed by this as a whole.

If I was to be extremely, brutally honest: I don't think this can really work as a SCP. The core of the story is too focussed on -2 and his growth and evolution as a person for the detached, cold format forced by a SCP file to effectively tell his story. If this was a tale, from the perspective of -2, you'd be able to convey his despair a lot better, and how the testing ruins his mental health, and how he gradually gets better once they employ a psychologist; but since you can't really…show any of that, it'll likely never land.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

and tests on its protective abilities are to be conducted monthly.
Every two months.

I would make the 'every two months' be more clearly something that was edited into the sentence for a time perhaps; though, there's likely not an easy way to do that: perhaps "and tests on its protective abilities are to be conducted monthly every two months." would be the best way

No more tests are to be conducted on SCP-XXXX without Dr Morter's approval and SCP-XXXX-2 is to have weekly meetings with Dr. Young from the Psychology and parapsychology departementdepartment.

This should be two sentences; the before/after around the first "and" are too separate for this to flow nicely together, and it feels like the first part would fit more neatly in the previous paragraph.

I'm also generally pretty against putting in specific people in ConProcs as opposed to roles (e.g. I'd use 'without approval from the Site Director' instead of 'without Dr Morter's approval') largely because what happens if Morter is e.g. killed or retires or w/e.

Psychological help should also be provided to SCP-XXXX-2 on demand.

I'm not necessarily sure about 'on demand' here; it feels a little vague and a little ripe for abuse and I kinda feel like the previous sentence covers this concept well enough.

SCP-XXXX-1 consists of 5 stuffed animals, belonging to SCP-XXXX-2, designated SCP-XXXX-1-A to SCP-XXXX-1-E.

You open the description referring to -1, which doesn't feature in the ConProcs, and also never describe a base SCP-XXXX thing during the description: it feels like the designation changed mid drafting and the rest of the article needs updating to take this into account.

IMO: whatever the first sentence of your description describes should be the base anomaly which the story is centred upon; in this case the humanoid. It should also be the hook: you want to hint at something interesting to make a reader go 'yes, I want to know more about this'.

SCP-XXXX-2 is a Caucasian Canadian adult male presenting severe signs of depression.

does -2 come from Canada or Caucasus? if you mean the male is white, say 'white Canadian' instead.

SCP-XXXX-2's anomaly manifests when it faces a situation of fear or distress before coming in contact withwhile not in the presence of at least one SCP-XXXX-1 entityinstance.

The current phrasing felt vague about the relation between the fear and the -1 instance and anomalous effects activating: specifically in that it implies that there's a period between 'exposed to fear' and 'activation of anomalous effects' where the bear could be applied whilst also being vague about how long that is. The change of entity to instance is cos 'entity' implies something alive, and not like, a regular teddy bear.

I don't like the start: 'anomaly manifests' feels needlessly vague about what happens here and I would prefer something like: "SCP-XXXX-2 manifests a protective sphere" as an opening here.

While the sphere is present, nothing is able to enter nor exit the sphere, with the exception of other SCP-XXXX-1 objects

The earlier phrasing implies -1 can't be present for the sphere to form; so the 'other' feels iffy here.

looses contact with every SCP-XXXX-1 entities.

same for this; the phrasing of the activation implies the sphere only occurs when there's no contact.

SCP-XXXX-2 also has a behavior of coming in contact with the most SCP-XXXX-1 possible during these events, even though this has no real effect on its abilities.

'this has no real effect on its abilities' feels super unclinical and I just, generally don't like this sentence as a whole?

Per 12/21/2020, SCP-XXXX-2 has accepted its anomalous property as its own, but still needs SCP-XXXX-1 objects to activate it.

This should really refer to an incident that happened rather than a date; or at least be 'After 12/21/2020,….'

He was apprehended by psychological staff, before being taken to site 43.

'psychological staff' feels iffy here cos it doesn't really seem like they should be doing this. Also site designations are always in the format of 'Site-43', with the capital and the hyphen.

The following interview was conducted by Dr Morter, assigned as lead researcher for SCP-XXXX, upon SCP-XXXX's arrival at the site:

You're missing an empty line between the previous paragraph and this one.

Do you know why you find yourself here?

This feels like a really weird question to ask because I'm struggling to see a situation where the answer isn't 'no'?

You are in the SCP Foundation, we will be containing and doing tests on you because you manifest an anomaly, which could be a danger for other people and yourself if aknowledged by too many outside of our organisation.

'acknowledged' is the correct spelling but there's something about this whole spiel that feels…really iffy and I'm not sure what. It flows weirdly, I think, but I'm not sure why.

Do you mean my animals' protection?

It feels odd, to me, for someone to refer to their stuffed toys as "my animals'"

Dr Morter is seen writing down some notes.

I'd cut this; we can assume that he is taking down notes where relevant and this doesn't like…add to the knowledge we've seen in any way? Like, it doesn't characterise Morter more or indicate he's realised something or anything, so it just feels…extraneous?

Also, by our Ethics Comitee's new recommandationsdue to the Ethics Committee's new recommendations concerning human SCPs I must ask you if you had someone you wanted to talk to one last time, before they get amnesticized and forget about you.

This feels like a really bad recommendation for the EC to make

Almost inaudibly. Its head is now lowered, facing the ground.

This flows weirdly: I would describe it's posture first and then say almost inaudibly; but I'd also probably use more words to describe it maybe? I'm not sure.

Louder, but the sound is muffled by SCP-XXXX-2's arms, which'swhich it's head is now between, laid on the table.

Something about this feels kinda iffy but I can't quite place why.

Until guards arrived in the interrogation room, SCP-XXXX-2 stayed in the same position for 3 minutes

Why did it take the guards three minutes to arrive at the room? It feels like there should be guards literally outside the door in case of emergency.

SCP-XXXX-2 seems to believe the sphere does not come from him, but SCP-XXXX-1-A to -E

The description and the interview already covered all this, so we don't like, actually need this whole section.

the agent shoots on the sphere in a way that could not hurt SCP-XXXX-2.

simply stopped is course when touchingit touched the sphere, seemingly loosing all of its speed upon contact with it.

We don't need to be told it lost all it's speed upon contact cos 'stopped when it touched the sphere' conveys that.

Analysis

This section (up to the italics) conveys no new information and could be cut.

SCP-XXXX-2 tried putting it downout without taking any SCP-XXXX-1 in his hands,

'without picking up an SCP-XXXX-1 instance' would be less janky than 'without taking any SCP-XXXX-1 in his hands'

until it started spreading around him. He then ran and sat in the only untouched corner

This doesn't create a clear picture of the fire: 'spreading around him' implies 'encircled' to me, so there being an 'untouched corner' feels, weird?

with SCP-XXXX-1 objects in his arms while hyperventilating, the sphere appearing the instant he touched SCP-XXXX-1-C.

I… don't really like how this is phrased. There's a clear image of him unmoving, slumped in a corner, with toys in his arms; and the idea of the sphere appearing when he touches -1-C feels weird because like….he's already touching them all?

The moment the fire touched the sphere, it evaporated into water vapour

'evaporation' is a specific thing in chemistry and I'm not sure fire can do that?

It's the third test and it still went horribly after the procedure ended.

'went horribly after the procedure ended' feels…iffy? It feels too much like you're telling us about bad things instead of showing us them.

regarding SCP-XXXX-2 are to be stopped until Dr. Morter approves of itthem.

'reapproves' might be better than 'approves' too

+ Addendum XXXX.C : Incident report : Incident XXXX-2.1

This is a janky ass title; I feel like you need to settle on giving this either an incident title or an addendum title instead of doing both.

I'd also shove this into a quoteblock too.

SCP-XXXX-2 is seen bashing his head against the wall of his cell while holding SCP-XXXX-1 objects, seemingly attempting to [EXPUNGED].

Why is this expunged? It's pretty clear that this is a suicide attempt from context; and so the data being hidden to the person reading the file feels weird as a baseline. But expungement is a step further: this data has been destroyed. It no longer exists, not even in the highest clearance version of this file. So it doesn't really like, make sense in universe and it doesn't really do anything out of universe other than blunten the impact of what you're saying so I'd just…use the word.

I'm concussioned.

'concussed'

I will answer to your question today, because I'm so done with you people that I don't even care about what you will do to me next. How good could I [EXPUNGED] be?

You're allowed to swear in a SCP article.

a [EXPUNGED] looserloser that saw talked to nobody.

Looks like my situation hasn't changed huh?

45 seconds of silence take place between the SCP and the doctor, while SCP-XXXX-2 cries, his hands on his face.

They aren't 'seconds of silence' if -2 is crying; and this is implied to be an audio transcript (from the 'Audio recorded' in the foreword), so how do they know from the recording what the SCP was doing?

without my approbation

'approbation' isn't like, incorrect here but it feels…like an odd choice of words.

ShortSmall— silence.

Ideally you'd specify a duration here over saying 'short' but *shrugs*

Upon a demand made by SCP-XXXX-2 to Dr. Young

This feels really iffy because like…we don't actually learn what the demand is? Did -2 just demand to see Morter? It should explicitly say what it was imo.
